1: Chapter 1: A Visitor on a Rainy Night

Rain had been falling over Qingshi for three solid days. Lin Xiaoyu’s elder sister, Chuntian, had gone to the capital, and ever since, Lin Xiaoyu had been left to run the little apothecary in town all by herself.
After dark, she shut the doors and windows, counted the day’s takings, snuffed the oil lamp, and went upstairs.
She had only just lain down when urgent knocking sounded from downstairs, followed by a man’s voice: “Is anyone there?”
Outside stood a young man soaked from head to toe, a bloodstained strip of cloth wrapped around his left arm. He said his name was Bai Yun and that he belonged to the Azure Dragon Society.
“I need my wound bandaged,” Bai Yun said quietly. “I can pay. Will three thousand five hundred copper coins be enough?”
He drew a letter wrapped in oiled paper from his coat. “This letter must reach Qingfeng before May eighteenth.”
As she bandaged his wound, he gave a rueful smile. “If my fiancée knew I was knocking on a girl’s door in the middle of the night, she’d definitely be jealous.”
Lin Xiaoyu did not accept his money. She only said, “At first light tomorrow, I’ll take you up the mountain.”
2: It was just dawn when the two of them set out. Lin Xiaoyu carried a bamboo basket holding dried rations, medicinal herbs, and an old umbrella.

Halfway up the mountain, they encountered Zhou Dashan, an old man chopping firewood. He set down his axe and lowered his voice, saying that three strangers had stopped at the entrance to town the previous evening and asked about an injured young man.
“Xiaoyu, you two should take the mountain trail,” Zhou Dashan said. “It isn’t safe on the main road.” Lin Xiaoyu thanked him.
The narrow trail was slick underfoot. Lin Xiaoyu walked in front, placing her feet carefully with every step. Bai Yun followed behind without a word.

At noon, the rain stopped, and the mist among the mountains slowly dispersed. Far ahead, the roof of Qingfeng came into view. A nun stood at the gate. Her name was Zhao Qiuyue, and she handled guest reception for the temple.
Zhao Qiuyue took the letter, glanced at the red seal on its closure, and nodded. “The abbot has been waiting for this letter for 2 years.”
Bai Yun said to Lin Xiaoyu, “I owe you my life.” Lin Xiaoyu laughed. “Then when you next visit, help me repair the roof of the medicine shop.” Bai Yun stayed at Qingfeng.
At dusk, Lin Xiaoyu descended the mountain alone. By the time she reached home, it was dark. She lit the lamp and sat behind the counter for a long time.
